key: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person; but let him devise means, that he that is banished be not an outcast from him.
s: Sent by Joab, the woman of Tekoa turns her tale toward Absalom; Radak, on 14:14, reads it as a plea to lessen bloodshed, since all must die, and the devising as God’s laws, which spare a killer where there are no witnesses and warning.

evidence.words: כלנו נמות ואין על האדם להרבות שפיכות דם אלא למעטו כמו שיוכל ואם יהרוג אדם חבירו לא צוה המקום להרגו אם לא הרגו במזיד בעדים ובהתראה כדי למעט שפיכות הדם ואם הרגו שוגג צוה שיגלה עד זמן ידוע ולא יהרגו אותו אפילו הרגו מזיד אם אין שם עדים והתראה וז"ש וחשב מחשבות לבלתי ידח ממנו נדח אלהים חשב מחשבות ושם משפטים לבלתי ידח ההורג
evidence.gloss: [Radak, on 14:14, ‘neither doth God respect any person’:] We all shall die, and a man ought not to multiply bloodshed but lessen it as far as he can; if a man kills his fellow, God did not command that he be killed unless he killed wilfully, with witnesses and warning, so as to lessen bloodshed; if he killed in error, He commanded exile for a set time and that he not be killed; nor is he killed even for a wilful killing where there are no witnesses and warning; and this is ‘let him devise means, that he that is banished be not an outcast from him’: God devised means and set laws so that the killer be not banished.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref 2 Samuel 14:14 and at [276,14] match; 41 words, one unit). Read Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David on all of chapter 14 in the packet (no Midrash Rabbah on 2 Samuel). Radak on 14:14 says all must die, so man should lessen bloodshed, not multiply it; God commanded death only for a wilful killing with witnesses and warning, exile for an error, and no death for a wilful killing without witnesses and warning; and the devising is God setting laws so the killer be not banished. The sentence carries exactly that, without drift; it gives Radak’s first reading (he adds a second, applying the devising to the king), which is his. Plain sense fits 14:1 to 13 (Joab sends to Tekoa for a wise woman, whose tale at 14:13 turns to the king’s banished one). Killing and law are stated plainly. entry-check ok.
